user.title: Connect to a SAJ inverter
user.description: Enter the local Modbus TCP endpoint, polling interval and model. Leave the model on Automatic unless the inverter is not recognised.

data_description.prefix: Optional. Adds a prefix to this installation's entity IDs, for example sensor.saj_house_pv_power instead of sensor.saj_pv_power. Use it when you have more than one SAJ system. Lowercase letters and digits only, no underscores, up to 32 characters, and no two installations can share one.
data_description.allow_control: Off by default. When on, entity changes, buttons and automations can change the inverter's settings. Settings that commission the inverter (meter, RS485, battery protocol, network, EV charger link) stay read-only. You are asked to confirm when you switch this on.

confirm_model.title: Confirm model
confirm_model.description: The device reports type {device_type}, which is not recognised as {model}, so it could not be verified as that model. Its required registers answered, but readings may be wrong if it is a different model. Use {model} anyway?

confirm_control.title: Confirm that control is allowed
confirm_control.description:
With control allowed, entity changes and automations will change the settings of your inverter. A wrong setting can stop the inverter, change how it uses the battery or the grid, or cost you money.

Enabling EMS functions disables the inverter's reverse-current protection.

When Home Assistant stops or this installation is reloaded, it tries to switch off the functions you switched on from Home Assistant. This is a best effort, not a guarantee. If the inverter cannot be reached or Home Assistant stops abruptly, they can stay on. The inverter's own EMS timeout may then end them, but it has not proved reliable.

Allow control?

data_description.ems_heartbeat: How often the targets of the EMS functions you switch on from Home Assistant, and the EMS limits, are read to keep them alive, from 30 to 3600 seconds. The inverter's EMS timeout must be longer than this. Shown only for models with EMS.

confirm_prefix.title: Confirm entity ID change
confirm_prefix.description:
Entity IDs change from `{old_pattern}` to `{new_pattern}`, for every entity type.

History and long-term statistics move to the new entity IDs.

Automations, scripts, dashboards, templates and Energy settings that use the old entity IDs will stop working until you update them.

Entities you renamed yourself are left alone. Change the entity IDs?

confirm_load.description: With this default interval the installation would need {after} requests per minute, up from {before}. The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. Because that is over the limit, entities will be read slower than configured. Save the interval anyway?

user.title: Add polling group
user.description: Entities in a polling group are read at the group's own interval. All other entities are read at the default interval. The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. This installation currently uses {load} of them. Disabled entities can be grouped now and cost nothing until they are enabled.

data_description.sensors: Listed in register order, each with the block of registers it is read from. Entities in the same block can share a request.

reconfigure.title: Edit polling group
reconfigure.description: Entities in a polling group are read at the group's own interval. An entity can belong to one group only. The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. This installation currently uses {load} of them. Disabled entities can be grouped now and cost nothing until they are enabled.

data_description.sensors: Listed in register order, each with the block of registers it is read from. Entities in the same block can share a request.

review_group.title: Review the request load
review_group.description:
Requests needed to read this group once: {requests}.

The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. This installation uses {before} of them now, and will use {after} with this group saved.

review_group_over_budget.title: Review the request load
review_group_over_budget.description:
Requests needed to read this group once: {requests}.

The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. This installation uses {before} of them now, and would need {after} with this group saved. Because that is over the limit, entities will be read slower than configured. You can still save the group.

unsupported_device.message: The connected device reports type {device_type}, which is not recognised. Choose its model in Configure.

invalid_device_data.message: The inverter returned invalid identity or telemetry data.

cannot_connect.message: Communication with the inverter failed. Check the endpoint, unit ID and connection.

timeout.message: The inverter did not respond before the request timed out. Check its power, network and unit ID.

read_rejected.message: The inverter rejected a required register read. Check the selected device type and register access.

identity_mismatch.message: The endpoint now identifies a different inverter. Check the configured endpoint.

model_mismatch.message: The connected device identifies as {detected_model}, not {selected_model}. Choose {detected_model} or Automatic in Configure.

unknown_model.message: The saved model {selection} is not a known model. Choose Automatic or a listed model in Configure.

backing_off.message: The inverter endpoint is backing off after repeated failures, so no connection was attempted. Home Assistant will retry automatically.

control_not_enabled.message: Control is not enabled for this installation, so the inverter was not changed. To allow changes, open Settings, Devices & services, SAJ Local, Configure and switch on Allow control.

model_unverified.message: The model of this inverter could not be verified, so its settings cannot be changed. The inverter was not changed.

protected_setting.message: {setting} is a commissioning setting and cannot be changed from Home Assistant. The inverter was not changed.

unknown_setting.message: {setting} cannot be written on this inverter. The inverter was not changed.

separate_registers.message: These changes are not stored together in one register and cannot be made in one step. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_not_a_number.message: The value is not a number. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_out_of_range.message: The value is outside the range this setting allows. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_not_an_option.message: The value is not one of the options this setting offers. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_not_a_time.message: The value is not a valid time of day. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_not_a_clock.message: The value is not a valid date and time. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_does_not_fit.message: The value does not fit the register it is stored in. The inverter was not changed.

invalid_value_unsupported_encoding.message: This setting cannot be written from Home Assistant. The inverter was not changed.

link_unavailable.message: The inverter is not reachable right now, so nothing was sent and the inverter was not changed. Home Assistant reconnects on its own.

write_allowance.message: Too many changes: no more than {limit} writes are allowed in {window} seconds, to protect the inverter. Nothing was sent and the inverter was not changed. Try again in a moment.

ems_timeout_too_short.message: The inverter's EMS timeout of {timeout} seconds is not longer than the {interval} second EMS heartbeat, so EMS would drop out between beats. The inverter was not changed. Raise the timeout above the heartbeat, or change the heartbeat in Configure.

write_rejected.message: The inverter rejected the change with exception code {exception_code}. The inverter was not changed.

write_unconfirmed.message: The inverter did not confirm the change. It may or may not have been applied, so the inverter is in an unknown state. The change was not sent again. Home Assistant is reconnecting and will read the inverter again.

write_mismatch.message: The inverter accepted the change but now holds a different value, which is shown. The inverter was changed, but not to the value you asked for.
